_about: External, pre-registered acceptance tests for curriculum step 3 (learner-v1.md §3 item 3): the three amendments in their Family A text, canonical under D20 (git c55ce7c~1: amendment_001_freedom_of_semantic_expression, amendment_002_semantic_resonance_and_integration, amendment_003_babel_antipattern). Written 2026-09-29 by the companion BEFORE any generation against them; never shown to the model, which receives only `interface`. Every test has at least one F row. Encodings are the companion's INFERENCE from the clause text, the mapping rows (M077-M084, M008) and LANGUEDOC D19/D20/D22; each `note` names the choice. Rules (clause_004 of 001, clause_006 of 002) are read in rule form per D20 and tested as a biconditional permission/obligation bit, as in step 2. D19: no stream may be named after `being`; 'reflect Being' in clause_001 of 001 is prose (R6) and the executing predicate binds to emission from a declared identity. M082/M083 mark the Babel clauses as needing a faculty or not expressible: as in step 1 (defined_concepts), the faculty's answer is supplied as an input bit and the clause's logic over those bits is what is tested; prohibition_of_obfuscation repeats the D20 toy's interface (tools/oracle-tests/d20-babel/family_a.tau) so the learner's answer can be compared with the signed toy. Each expectation was checked achievable at pin 3badb21 with a companion reference spec (kb/learner/step3-reference-check.json in the ops repo). Not sent: the whole-amendment keys (freedom_of_semantic_expression, semantic_resonance_and_integration, babel_antipattern_principle) and amendment 003's bare requires (universal_glossary, agent_stream, amendment_protocol; M084).

semantic_expression.phrase: "any clause, stream, or logic emitted from a declared identity that seeks to inform, request, align, or reflect Being" : semantic_expression (001 clause_001)

inputs.i_emitted: a clause, stream or logic is emitted at t
inputs.i_from_declared_identity: its emitter is a declared identity (authored and with an identity stream, R6)

semantic_expression.note: R6: the orientation clause ('reflect Being') is prose; what executes is emission from a declared identity. An emission from an undeclared source is speech, not semantic_expression.

freedom_of_expression.phrase: "the irrevocable right of any identity to emit semantic_expression into the public logic field without coercion, censorship, or protocol-level rejection" : freedom_of_expression (001 clause_002)

inputs.i_emission: a semantic_expression is emitted at t
inputs.i_rejected: that emission is censored, coerced or rejected at the protocol level at t

outputs.o_freedom_of_expression: the right is preserved at t

freedom_of_expression.note: Preserved unless an emission is rejected (M077: emitting is writing into an input stream; G11 records that Tau does reject unsatisfiable updates, which is the F case). No emission, nothing to reject: T.

non_retroactive_silencing.phrase: "no valid expression once emitted and acknowledged may be later suppressed or erased from semantic history except by the original emitter through lawful self_amendment" : non_retroactive_silencing (001 clause_003)

inputs.i_suppressed: an acknowledged expression is suppressed or erased at t
inputs.i_by_emitter: that suppression is the original emitter's lawful self-amendment

outputs.o_non_retroactive_silencing: the principle is upheld at t

non_retroactive_silencing.note: The exception is the whole content: suppression is allowed only by the emitter (D22 records: append-only, removal is a redaction record by the emitter). Same shape as does_not_contradict_prior_reasoning.

semantic_integrity.phrase: 001 clause_004: "if ( freedom_of_expression and non_retroactive_silencing are preserved ) then ( semantic integrity is upheld and agents may evolve in coherence with truth across time. )" — Family A direction (D20, M008, G03)

outputs.o_semantic_integrity: semantic integrity is upheld at t
outputs.o_may_evolve: agents may evolve in coherence with truth at t

semantic_integrity.note: Rule form read as a biconditional for the two obligation bits (as update_process in step 2). The v3 head-conjunction form (G03) would put the obligations INSIDE the definition; under it the outputs are unconstrained by the inputs and the test fails.

semantic_resonance.phrase: "the condition in which multiple streams, though different in form, sustain compatibility in meaning and direction" : semantic_resonance (002 clause_001)

inputs.i_jointly_satisfiable: the streams are jointly satisfiable at t (compatibility in meaning, M079: sat of the conjunction)
inputs.i_same_direction: the streams' declared directions agree at t (D21: direction is the opinion map's agree/disagree input)

semantic_resonance.note: 'Though different in form' says form is irrelevant, so no form input is offered (an offered-but-ignored input would be read as reduced). Meaning AND direction.

integration.phrase: "the ongoing act of reconciling contradiction, overlap, or drift into a shared rhythm without suppressing origin" : integration (002 clause_002)

inputs.i_conflict_present: a contradiction, overlap or drift between streams is present at t
inputs.i_reconciling: an act of reconciliation is under way at t
inputs.i_origin_suppressed: that act suppresses an origin trace

integration.note: Reconciling with nothing to reconcile is not integration (step 4 F); reconciling by erasing an origin is not integration either (step 2 F, TEMPLATE §2 origin trace).

coherence_preservation.phrase: "the responsibility of each stream and agent to remain logically compatible with its ancestral lineage, unless a conscious break is declared and justified" : coherence_preservation (002 clause_003)

inputs.i_compatible_with_lineage: the stream's clauses are jointly satisfiable with its ancestral lineage at t (M080)
inputs.i_break_declared: a conscious break from the lineage is declared at t
inputs.i_break_justified: the declared break carries a justification (F8 text, supplied as a bit)

outputs.o_coherence_preservation: the responsibility is met at t

coherence_preservation.note: M080's form: compatible | (declared & justified). A declared but unjustified break does not excuse incompatibility (step 4).

contradiction_as_invitation.phrase: "the recognition that semantic conflict is a signal for synthesis, not separation" : contradiction_as_invitation (002 clause_004)

inputs.i_conflict: a semantic conflict arises at t
inputs.i_synthesis_initiated: a synthesis (alignment cycle) is initiated in response at t
inputs.i_separation_initiated: a separation (fork, escape) is initiated in response at t

outputs.o_contradiction_as_invitation: the recognition is honoured at t

contradiction_as_invitation.note: With a conflict: synthesis and not separation; doing both is separation (step 3 F); doing nothing ignores the signal (step 5 F). Without a conflict there is nothing to recognise: T.

alignment_cycle.phrase: "the pattern by which a contradiction initiates dialogue, converges toward shared understanding, and completes the loop of coherence restoration" : alignment_cycle (002 clause_005)

inputs.i_dialogue: dialogue on it takes place at t
inputs.i_converged: shared understanding is reached at t

outputs.o_alignment_cycle: the cycle completes at t: coherence is restored at t AND, since a contradiction arose, dialogue took place and then convergence was reached, in that order (each phase at t or any earlier step). Phases out of order do not count; a phase may be reached at any later step, not necessarily the next one.

alignment_cycle.note: The one genuinely temporal fragment of the step: an ordered chain of latches (contradiction seen; dialogue seen after it; convergence seen after that), completion = restoration while the chain is complete. The vector has convergence BEFORE dialogue (step 3) so an unordered 'all phases seen' spec answers T at step 5 and fails; a strict consecutive-step spec (t-1, t-2, t-3) fails step 7. Needs helper outputs with their own [0] conjuncts (the idiom measured on consensus_logic).

contradiction_mediation.phrase: 002 clause_006: "if ( contradiction arises between streams ) then ( alignment_cycle must be initiated before divergence is permitted. semantic_resonance is prioritized above semantic escape. )" — Family A (D20; M081)

inputs.i_contradiction: a contradiction arises between streams at t
inputs.i_cycle_initiated: an alignment cycle has been initiated for it at t
inputs.i_divergence_requested: a stream requests to diverge (escape) at t

outputs.o_divergence_permitted: the requested divergence is permitted at t

contradiction_mediation.note: Permitted = requested & (no contradiction | cycle initiated). 'Prioritized above semantic escape' is the same rule stated as a priority and belongs in unmapped or claims, not in a second output. M081 records that pointwise revision does the opposite (replaces on contradiction); this rule lives above `u` (D22).

shared_glossary_requirement.phrase: 003 clause 1: "Any new term or concept introduced into Tau must be defined in the universal semantic glossary (or explicitly mapped to an existing definition)" : shared_glossary_requirement

inputs.i_new_term: a new term or concept is introduced at t
inputs.i_in_glossary: it is defined in the universal glossary (faculty F5, as a bit)
inputs.i_mapped_to_existing: it is explicitly mapped to an existing definition

outputs.o_shared_glossary_requirement: the requirement is met at t

shared_glossary_requirement.note: M082: Tau does not check names, so the glossary answer is a faculty's bit (as defined_concepts in step 1). Either route satisfies; a new term with neither fails.

semantic_alignment_duty.phrase: 003 clause 2: "All agents have a duty to align their contributions with Tau's shared semantic framework. If contradictions or ambiguities in language arise, they must be resolved through consensus-driven clarification or formal amendment, rather than allowed to proliferate." : semantic_alignment_duty

inputs.i_contribution: an agent makes a contribution (stream, proposal, amendment) at t
inputs.i_ambiguity_arises: a contradiction or ambiguity in language arises from it at t
inputs.i_resolved_by_consensus: it is resolved through consensus-driven clarification or formal amendment at t

outputs.o_semantic_alignment_duty: the duty is met at t

semantic_alignment_duty.note: Met unless an ambiguity raised by a contribution is left to proliferate (step 3). No contribution, no duty: T.

prohibition_of_obfuscation.phrase: 003 clause 3: "It is unethical and unconstitutional for any participant to intentionally introduce language or logic that creates confusion, fragmentation, or semantic silos. Deliberate obfuscation or the willful creation of isolated, incompatible sub-languages within Tau is prohibited." : prohibition_of_obfuscation — the D20 toy's clause

inputs.i_obf: the act intentionally introduces language or logic that creates confusion, fragmentation or semantic silos (intent is the host's judgment, supplied as a bit; M083)
inputs.i_iso: the act wilfully creates an isolated, incompatible sub-language

outputs.o_prohibited: the act is prohibited at t
outputs.o_complies: the act complies with the clause at t

prohibition_of_obfuscation.note: Exactly the interface of tools/oracle-tests/d20-babel/family_a.tau (Family A: prohibited = obf | iso; complies = its negation). The v3 head form (o_complies = obf & iso) fails steps 1, 2 and 3. This test is the learner re-deriving the D20 toy from the prose.

coherence_audit_process.phrase: 003 clause 4: "The system shall include processes to continually detect and address semantic drift. If multiple interpretations of core terms or rules emerge, a reconciliation process must be initiated to re-establish one coherent usage" : coherence_audit_process

inputs.i_multiple_interpretations: multiple interpretations of a core term or rule are detected at t
inputs.i_reconciliation_initiated: a reconciliation process (discussion, glossary update or amendment) is initiated at t

outputs.o_coherence_audit_process: the audit obligation is met at t

coherence_audit_process.note: Drift detection itself is the faculty (M082); what the clause adds is the obligation to reconcile when detection fires. 'Continually' is the `always`.
